title: Which spot balances the distances to all four dots?
description: Four dots stand on a number line at ten, ten, eleven and seventeen. The board finds the mean, then adds the distances on each side of it, and does the same for two other spots. Keeko's doubt is that the mean is always halfway between the smallest and the largest value.
teaching_notes: One idea: the mean is the one spot where the distances to the dots on its left add up to the distances to the dots on its right. Watch for students who think the mean is the midpoint of the two end values.

source: Show that the mean of 10, 10, 11 and 17 balances the distanc
video_script.why: The child sees the mean as the balance spot of the distances on a number line, not only as a sum divided by a count.
video_script.substitution: Place each number as a dot on a number line, then add the distances from a chosen spot to the dots on its left and on its right.
video_script.anchor: a number line with four dots at ten, ten, eleven and seventeen, the two tens stacked
video_script.wrong_answer: the mean is always halfway between the smallest and the largest value
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the mean is the midpoint of the two end values. Halfway between ten and seventeen is thirteen and a half, but the mean is twelve, so the middle of the ends is not the balance.

final_answer.value: Only 12 balances the distances; 13 and 11 do not
final_answer.spoken: only twelve balances the distances, and thirteen and eleven do not

hold_back: Answer: Only 12 balances the distances; 13 and 11 do not
never_show: the final answer line before the answer beat
maths_rules: spot 12: left distances 2 + 2 + 1 = 5; right distance 17 - 12 = 5; equal
spot 13: left distances 3 + 3 + 2 = 8; right distance 17 - 13 = 4; not equal
spot 11: left distances 1 + 1 + 0 = 2; right distance 17 - 11 = 6; not equal
Keeko's doubt: halfway between 10 and 17 is (10 + 17) / 2 = 13.5, which is not the mean 12
video_script.design: One idea: the mean balances the distances. The number line stays from ground to the end of the idea part. Wrong idea: the mean is the midpoint of the end values.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the mean is always halfway between the smallest and the largest value.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Halfway between ten and seventeen is thirteen and a half, but the mean is twelve.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The mean balances every distance, so every dot counts, not only the two ends.
